search_filter.ai_search.help: Enter the prompt condition including the column names and values to return the rows which match the condition.
search_filter.ai_search.label: Advance Filter Condition Prompt
search_filter.ai_search.prompt: Generate a JavaScript if condition using Google Sheet column names based on the user's search condition and the provided sample sheet data. You must include the || '' fallback to handle empty cells and undefined values safely. When a dynamic path is used in the condition, you MUST wrap the path in single quotes. Example: If the user gives the prompt "Compare the sheet row's Status column with ${context.req.body.status}.", the output should be exactly: String((row['Status'] || '').trim()).toLowerCase() === String(('${context.req.body.status}' || '').trim()).toLowerCase(). Note: The sheet can have the column name or column letters. If you can see the key name as a column name, not letters, then do not guess the column letter.
search_filter.ai_search.placeholder: Email is email@domain.com or phone is..

• Multiple rows — [["Alice", 25], ["Bob", 30]]
• Formula — =TODAY()

• Single row: [["Alice", 25, "Manager"]]
• Multiple rows: [["Alice", 25], ["Bob", 30]]
• Formula: =TODAY()
updates.values.label: Values

value_input_option.help:
Controls how your values are interpreted when written to the sheet.

• User Entered — values are parsed as if a user typed them. Formulas like =SUM(A1:A5) get calculated, dates get formatted automatically.
• Raw — values are stored exactly as provided with no parsing or formatting applied.

updates.major_dimension.label: Write Direction

include_values_in_response.label: Include Updated Values in Response

response_value_render_option.help:

• Formatted Value — numbers and dates shown exactly as displayed in the sheet (default)
• Unformatted Value — raw computed values without any sheet formatting applied
• Formula — returns the formula text itself rather than the computed result
